writing.prompt: Directions: Suppose you have attended a lecture delivered by a famous scholar. Write a report to the campus newspaper, summarizing its most important points. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
writing.sample: A Report on Professor Li's Lecture Last week our university had the honor of hosting a lecture by Professor Li, a well-known scholar in education, who spoke to a full hall of students on how to grow during our college years. The speaker raised several important points. First, he pointed out that lifelong learning is the key to coping with a rapidly changing world, arguing that the knowledge we gain today may soon be out of date. He went on to emphasize that we should turn our curiosity into action and never be afraid of making mistakes, since real growth comes from trying rather than waiting. To illustrate this, he cited his own failures as the most valuable lessons in his career. The lecture was warmly received, and many students felt newly inspired to take charge of their own learning. In short, it offered all of us valuable insight into making the most of our college life.

transcript.en: African leaders plan to turn the continent into a continent without borders. They will introduce a single passport policy, allowing free movement between countries. The idea from the African Union has been modeled on the EU Schengen free movement deal. Europe has abolished many internal borders. This enables visa-free movement across the continent. Currently, 13 African countries have visa-free deals in place with each other. These allow citizens to visit another country without a visa. Some countries offer visas on arrival. In contrast, Americans are able to travel to 20 of the continent's countries without a visa, or secure a visa on arrival. The African Union, which represents 54 states, wants to abolish the requirement of a visa for Africans visiting other African countries. It also wants to establish a free trade deal across the continent in the near future, as trade within the African continent costs more than any other region.
transcript.zh: 非洲领导人计划将该大陆变成一个无边界的大陆。他们将推行单一护照政策,允许各国之间自由流动。这一来自非洲联盟的想法是以欧盟申根自由流动协议为蓝本的。欧洲已经取消了许多内部边界,这使得整个大陆可以免签证自由流动。目前,13个非洲国家之间已经建立了免签证协议。这些协议允许公民无需签证即可访问另一个国家。一些国家提供落地签证。相比之下,美国人能够在无需签证或获得落地签证的情况下前往该大陆的20个国家。代表54个国家的非洲联盟希望取消非洲人访问其他非洲国家的签证要求。它还希望在不久的将来在整个大陆建立自由贸易协定,因为非洲大陆内部的贸易成本高于任何其他地区。

transcript.en: Researchers in Iceland found a new way of tackling climate change by pumping carbon dioxide underground and turning it into stone. Other carbon capture and storage methods store carbon dioxide as a gas. But problems include a high cost and concern about leaks. This new method of burying carbon dioxide and turning it into stone is cheaper and more secure, the Guardian reports. To turn carbon dioxide into stone, researchers with the CarbFix project pumped the gas into volcanic rock and sped up the natural process, in which the volcanic rock reacts with gas and forms carbon minerals. The gas turned into solid in just two years, much faster than the hundreds or thousands of years researchers had predicted. The research took place at Iceland's Hellisheidi power plant. Already, the project in Iceland has been increased in scale to bury 10,000 tons of carbon dioxide each year. One potential difficulty is that for each ton of carbon dioxide buried, the technique requires 25 tons of water. However, the lead researcher said sea water could be used.
transcript.zh: 冰岛的研究人员发现了一种应对气候变化的新方法，即将二氧化碳泵入地下并将其转化为石头。其他碳捕获和储存方法以气体形式储存二氧化碳。但问题包括成本高昂以及对泄漏的担忧。据《卫报》报道，这种埋藏二氧化碳并将其转化为石头的新方法更便宜、更安全。为了将二氧化碳转化为石头，CarbFix项目的研究人员将气体泵入火山岩中，并加速了火山岩与气体反应形成碳矿物的自然过程。气体仅在两年内就转化为固体,远快于研究人员预测的数百年或数千年。该研究在冰岛的Hellisheidi发电厂进行。冰岛的该项目规模已经扩大,每年可埋藏10,000吨二氧化碳。一个潜在的困难是,每埋藏一吨二氧化碳,该技术需要25吨水。然而,首席研究员表示可以使用海水。

transcript.en: People in France are keeping away from the narrow French stick loaf in favour of healthier, cheaper options, a millers' association has said. The National Association of French Millers says bread consumption is on the decline, with French people eating nine grams less than in the previous year. The association is concerned about the effects this trend will have on their trade and suggests three reasons why it is happening.
transcript.zh: 法国一家磨坊协会表示,法国人正在远离细长的法式棍子面包,转而选择更健康、更便宜的食品。法国全国磨坊协会称,面包消费量正在下降,法国人的食用量比前一年减少了9克。该协会对这一趋势将对其行业产生的影响表示担忧,并提出了造成这种情况的三个原因。

transcript.en: Firstly, the association cited changing diets, in particular, the switch to those low in calories, as a factor in the reduction of bread consumption. This could explain why the difference in consumption between genders is so big. Nowadays, men eat an approximate average of 140 grams of bread daily, whereas women eat 80 to 90 grams. The second reason they say is lifestyle changes in the country, with people dedicating less time to breakfast when bread would traditionally be eaten with butter and jam. Finally, the rising cost of bread is considered to be a factor, with the price of a French stick loaf increasing by nearly 25% in the last 10 years.
transcript.zh: 首先,该协会指出饮食习惯的改变,特别是转向低热量饮食,是面包消费量减少的一个因素。这可以解释为什么性别之间的消费差异如此之大。如今,男性平均每天吃大约140克面包,而女性吃80到90克。他们所说的第二个原因是该国生活方式的变化,人们用于早餐的时间减少了,而早餐传统上会搭配黄油和果酱吃面包。最后,面包价格上涨被认为是一个因素,法式棍子面包的价格在过去10年中上涨了近25%。

transcript.en: W: Next, please.
transcript.zh: W: 下一位，请。

transcript.en: M: Yes, I'd like to book two train tickets to London tomorrow morning, please.
transcript.zh: M: 好的，我想订两张明天早上去伦敦的火车票。

transcript.en: W: Okay. What time would you like to go?
transcript.zh: W: 好的。您想什么时候出发？

transcript.en: M: Well, after the rush hour, I think. We'd like to avoid the crowds if possible. So, probably sometime around 10 o'clock.
transcript.zh: M: 嗯，我想在高峰期之后吧。如果可能的话，我们想避开人群。所以，大概10点左右吧。

transcript.en: W: No problem. Just give me a minute. There's one here at 9:47, then one at 10:12, and then a third at 10:26.
transcript.zh: W: 没问题。稍等一下。这里有一班9点47分的，然后10点12分有一班，还有第三班10点26分的。

transcript.en: M: The one at 10:12 sounds good.
transcript.zh: M: 10点12分那班听起来不错。

transcript.en: W: All right. Would you like to sit in first or second class?
transcript.zh: W: 好的。您想坐头等舱还是二等舱？

transcript.en: M: Second class is fine. Thanks. Is there any chance we could have a window seat for one of those?
transcript.zh: M: 二等舱就可以。谢谢。有没有可能给我们其中一个安排靠窗的座位？

transcript.en: W: No problem. And I've booked those seats next to each other for you. The total price is 36 pounds, 50 cents. Is there anything else?
transcript.zh: W: 没问题。我已经给您订了相邻的座位。总价是36英镑50便士。还有其他需要吗？

transcript.en: M: Yes, actually, we'll be taking our bicycles with us. What is the arrangement for that? And will it cost extra?
transcript.zh: M: 有的，实际上我们会带着自行车一起去。这方面怎么安排？需要额外收费吗？

transcript.en: W: It's no extra cost. The price will be the same. All you need to do is wait at the far end of the platform. When the train arrives, tell the train guard where you're going, and he will help you secure the bicycles in the last carriage and give you a ticket. Then you can walk down through the train to your carriage and take your seats. When you arrive in London, hand the ticket to the guard and he will return the bicycles to you.
transcript.zh: W: 不需要额外费用。价格是一样的。您只需要在站台最远端等候。火车到达时，告诉列车员您要去哪里，他会帮您把自行车固定在最后一节车厢并给您一张票。然后您就可以穿过列车走到您的车厢就座。到达伦敦后，把票交给列车员，他会把自行车还给您。

transcript.en: M: Thank you for the information. That's very helpful.
transcript.zh: M: 谢谢您提供的信息。非常有帮助。

transcript.en: Love them or hate them, smartphones have become an integral part of our daily lives. But should they be left outside the classroom?
transcript.zh: 无论喜欢还是讨厌，智能手机已经成为我们日常生活中不可或缺的一部分。但它们应该被拒之于课堂之外吗？

transcript.en: Nick Gibb, Minister for School Standards in England, believes schools should ban their pupils from bringing in smartphones.
transcript.zh: 英格兰学校标准大臣Nick Gibb认为，学校应该禁止学生携带智能手机。

transcript.en: Astrid Natley, a secondary school math teacher, incorporates phones into her classroom. "My school doesn't have money for tablets," she says. "When students use their phones for research, they learn they have a powerful tool in their hands. If we stop children using phones, we're rejecting something they care about."
transcript.zh: 中学数学教师Astrid Natley在课堂上使用手机。她说："我的学校没有钱买平板电脑。当学生用手机做研究时，他们会意识到自己手中握有一个强大的工具。如果我们禁止孩子使用手机，我们就是在拒绝他们关心的东西。"

transcript.en: Meanwhile, Helen Lockhart, a registered nurse working for community education, supports a complete ban. "I'm banned from mobile use at work, and my phone must be handed in. If I'm caught with it in my pocket, I will be subject to disciplinary procedure, which will impact on my career. We need to teach children how to behave like the professionals they are striving to become."
transcript.zh: 与此同时，在社区教育部门工作的注册护士Helen Lockhart支持全面禁止。"我在工作时被禁止使用手机,而且必须上交手机。如果我被发现口袋里有手机,我将受到纪律处分,这会影响我的职业生涯。我们需要教会孩子们如何表现得像他们努力成为的专业人士。"

transcript.en: Richard Stone, an English teacher, thinks there should be a clear separation between school and home. "Students should do things differently in the two environments. Children are getting more than enough screen time in their lives without the need to bring their phone into the classroom. The internet is too easy and too unreliable a research tool, so let's leave phones and laptops at home, and show them a different world in their lessons—one of books and pens," he says.
transcript.zh: 英语教师Richard Stone认为学校和家庭之间应该有明确的界限。"学生在这两种环境中应该做不同的事情。孩子们在生活中已经有足够多的屏幕时间,没有必要把手机带进课堂。互联网作为研究工具过于便捷且不够可靠,所以让我们把手机和笔记本电脑留在家里,在课堂上向他们展示一个不同的世界——一个书本和笔的世界。"他说。

transcript.en: Kate, a six-year-old girl, helped her brother wash windows to get a reward promised by her mother, a purple doll that she wanted. She watched her mother order the doll online. The next day Kate asked if she could check the shipping status, so her mom clicked on the web page and then walked out of the room. Kate saw that her doll would be arriving the next afternoon, but then she noticed something else, suggestions about other dolls and toys she could order. 15 minutes and a few clicks later, with more than $350 worth of dolls in her cart, Kate placed the order and ran off to play.
transcript.zh: 六岁女孩Kate帮哥哥擦窗户，以获得母亲承诺的奖励——她想要的一个紫色玩偶。她看着母亲在网上订购这个玩偶。第二天Kate问能否查看物流状态，于是她妈妈点开网页后走出了房间。Kate看到她的玩偶将在第二天下午送达，但随后她注意到了别的东西——关于她可以订购的其他玩偶和玩具的推荐。15分钟和几次点击之后，购物车里装着价值超过350美元的玩偶，Kate下了单并跑去玩了。

transcript.en: The next day, while checking on another online order, her mother noticed a long list of dolls on the way. She was able to cancel two of them, but it was too late to cancel the rest. She told her daughter that they were going to be returned. When the packages arrived, Kate wanted to open them, but her parents said no. Instead of sending back the dolls, her father suggested giving them to the local children's hospital. So the next week, Kate's family loaded up their car and took all the dolls to the playroom at the children's hospital. Kate was depressed at first, but then she sat with some girl patients and they opened up all the boxes together, laughing and playing. She had a lot of fun and learned a really good lesson.
transcript.zh: 第二天，在查看另一个网上订单时，她母亲注意到了一长串在途的玩偶。她能够取消其中两个，但已经来不及取消其余的了。她告诉女儿这些玩偶将被退回。当包裹到达时，Kate想打开它们，但她父母说不行。她父亲建议把玩偶送给当地儿童医院，而不是退回去。于是下周，Kate一家装满了他们的车，把所有玩偶送到了儿童医院的游戏室。Kate起初很沮丧，但随后她和几个住院的女孩坐在一起，她们一起打开了所有盒子，笑着玩着。她玩得很开心，并学到了非常好的一课。

transcript.en: Can the date you were born affect how successful your life is? According to recent research done in Australia, the answer is yes. The researchers found that the time when a person starts school has an enduring impact on their lives. Those who are relatively old, compared to their classmates, have certain advantages over them. Previous research has found older students achieve better results. They are also more likely to attend university and become professional athletes, chief executives and even important politicians. But the Australian researchers wanted to discover what was driving these differences. They suspected older, more mature students obtained more self-confidence than their peers because they achieved better grades.
transcript.zh: 出生日期能否影响你的人生成功程度？根据澳大利亚最近进行的研究，答案是肯定的。研究人员发现，一个人开始上学的时间对其一生有持久的影响。那些与同学相比年龄相对较大的人比他们具有某些优势。先前的研究发现年龄较大的学生取得更好的成绩。他们也更有可能上大学，成为职业运动员、首席执行官甚至重要的政治家。但澳大利亚研究人员想要发现是什么驱动了这些差异。他们怀疑年龄较大、更成熟的学生因为取得更好的成绩而获得比同龄人更多的自信。

transcript.en: To test this out, they conducted two studies. One was with high school students and the other with more than a thousand Australian adults, age between 24 and 60 years old. In the first study more than 600 high school students were surveyed about their tendency to take risks and feel confident. In the second study, those born on both sides of the cutoff date for starting school were asked to complete online math questions and rate their performance. They were also asked about the risks they took while riding bicycles and managing their finances. The researchers found that older students displayed greater risk-taking tendencies. While risk-taking can be considered a negative attribute, it's also a characteristic of successful people, including athletes, political leaders and entrepreneurs.
transcript.zh: 为了验证这一点，他们进行了两项研究。一项针对高中生，另一项针对一千多名年龄在24至60岁之间的澳大利亚成年人。在第一项研究中，600多名高中生接受了关于他们冒险倾向和自信心的调查。在第二项研究中,那些出生在入学截止日期两侧的人被要求完成在线数学题并评估自己的表现。他们还被问及骑自行车和管理财务时所冒的风险。研究人员发现年龄较大的学生表现出更大的冒险倾向。虽然冒险可以被视为一种负面特质，但它也是成功人士的特征，包括运动员、政治领袖和企业家。

matching.title: Hyphenating your last name after marriage?

paragraphs.t: Congratulations on deciding to get married! While being married is great and wonderful, the act of getting married can be quite stressful. There is the planning of the ceremony itself, the merging( 合并) of two households and all of the details involved in that. You also have to take the time to apply for your marriage license and then decide whether or not you are going to keep your last name or change it.

This is where a lot of people have trouble. Once upon a time, it was just customary for a bride to take her groom's last name as her own and abandon her maiden name completely. The act of keeping her own last name was considered taboo(禁忌) and people's eyebrows would raise right off their faces when they found out that the bride was even considering something so radical. Over time, though, more and more women are deciding to keep their last names.

There are a lot of reasons to want to keep your own last name. Hopefully you have a supportive groom who understands why this idea is the most appealing to you. A lot of times, though, the act of keeping your name is still something that causes concern. Even if your groom is fine with it, his family (or your own) might not be so understanding.

There are a couple of ways to compromise on the issue. You could choose an entirely new last name for the two of you to share. This way neither of you gets "your" way and you both have to deal with the legalities of going through a name change. Most of the time, though, the most popular compromise is to hyphenate your last name and the last name of your groom. For example, if your groom's name is John Smith and your name is Kate Jones, you would name yourself Kate Jones-Smith or Kate Smith-Jones. This allows you to keep going by your own last name while legally adopting your husband's last name at the same time.

The compromise is the biggest reason that so many women choose to hyphenate their last names. It is a way of you keeping your own identity while also making your future husband happy. It allows you to stay connected to accomplishments that you achieved before you got married. For example, many women who choose to hyphenate do so partially because they have earned higher educational degrees and certifications under their maiden names. They might have also had things published or publicized and want to stay connected to that identity. Hyphenating your last name can help you bridge the gap between your personal and professional lives. Many women who opt to simply keep their own names do so because they don't want to give up all that they have accomplished professionally. Adopting their husband's last name makes it hard for them to claim ownership of these accomplishments personally because they happened under their "other" name.

While tradition is one thing, there isn't any logical reason to completely change your name. Keeping your name and joining it to your husband's through hyphenation is as legal as simply adopting his name or as simply keeping your own and leaving his out of the picture entirely.

Probably the most important reason to consider hyphenation is your identity. You've spent your whole life building your identity under a certain name. Obviously you will still be you even if you've taken on your husband's last name and omitted yours entirely. At the same time, your name is associated with the identity you've built up and hyphenation allows you to respect that while also respecting tradition and your husband's family's identity.

If you care about outside opinions on your name, you should know that a large portion of today's society is annoyed by the hyphenated name. Some people find it "snobby"(势利的) and others simply find it irritating because they have a hard time remembering which last name they are supposed to say first. Some people even believe that not simply adopting your husband's last name is a huge sign of disrespect and a lack of commitment.

It is possible that your future husband will find this choice offensive. Some men, regardless of how you might feel about such things, are traditionalists and feel that it is simply "right" for the woman to take the man's last name as her own. Whether your future husband insisting on your adopting his last name is a red flag to you or not, it is still something that you should take into consideration.

There are all sorts of reasons to hyphenate your name or not to hyphenate your name. The basis for each of these things, however, is whether or not you are willing to make a compromise when it comes to changing your name. The hyphenation is the epitome(体现) of a compromise. One spouse wants a complete name change. The other spouse wants no name change. Hyphenating the two names is a way for each person to, at least a little bit, "win" the argument.

And don't forget the legal stuff! Making the decision is just part of the process. From there you are going to have to legally change your name all over the place. You'll need to change your name at the bank, with social security, with your credit cards, on your driver's license, at the gym…everywhere. It's easy to get overwhelmed just thinking about it.

What matters, of course, is that the two of you are going to be happily married—hopefully for the rest of your lives. At the end of the day, whether you each keep your names, whether you come up with an entirely new name for the two of you to share or whether you hyphenate your current last names, what matters is that you love each other and are going to be joining your lives together. Try to remember that as you are staring at the application for your marriage license and filling out the portion that reads "name after you get married" (or whatever the legalese for that might be).

questions.s: Many people today still find name hyphenation upon marriage unacceptable.
As a compromise, a bride will in most cases adopt a name that combines the couple's last names.

Hyphenating names allows the bride to preserve her own identity while respecting tradition.
No matter what name the bride adopts, it is most important that the newlyweds truly love each other.
Legally speaking, the bride is free to choose whatever name she prefers.

careful.passage: It's good to be smart. After all, intelligent people earn more money, accumulate more wealth, and even live longer. But there's another side to the story. The brightest people and strongest leaders sometimes make errors others don't, especially in situations that require common sense. Travis Bradberry, president at TalentSmart, explained in his post Why Smart People Act So Stupid that "Rational thinking and intelligence don't tend to go hand in hand. Intelligent people are more prone to silly mistakes because of blind spots in how they use logic. These blind spots exist because smart people tend to be overconfident in their reasoning abilities." They are so used to being right and having quick answers that they don't even realise when they're making a mess by answering without thinking things through. A lifetime of praise leads smart people to develop too much faith in their intelligence and abilities. They often fail to recognise when they need help, and when they do recognise it, they tend to believe that no one else is capable of providing it. "It's hard for anyone to graciously accept the fact that they're wrong. It's even harder for smart people because they grow so used to being right all the time that it becomes a part of their identity," Bradberry wrote. "For smart people, being wrong can feel like a personal attack, and being right, a necessity." Smart people also have a hard time accepting feedback. They tend to undervalue the opinions of others, which means they have trouble believing that anyone is qualified to give them useful feedback. Not only does this tendency hinder their growth and performance, it can lead to harmful relationships, both personally and professionally. Smart people develop overachieving personalities because things come so easily to them. They simply don't understand how hard some people have to work to accomplish the same things, and because of that, they push people too hard. They set the bar too high, and when people take too long or don't get things quite right, they assume it's due to a lack of effort. So they push even harder.

careful.passage: Of the endless troubles that come with being driven from one's home country, losing educational certificates may seem small. But it isn't. Refugees who settle in other countries often find themselves unable to continue on their previous career path due to a new set of employer standards or skills requirements. To solve this problem, the U.S. State Department is posing a solution: online learning. The State Department will announce a partnership with an online education platform called Coursera. The platform will allow refugees worldwide to take thousands of online courses for free. "Coursera for Refugees" will be available for any non-profit group that supports refugees in any country, as well as individual refugees. They can apply for fully funded access to Coursera's course catalog, which means they can take all of the platform's classes and obtain professional certificates for free. The platform currently offers professor-led lectures on a broad range of topics, from data science to fashion design. As the world migrant crisis intensifies, employment is becoming a global concern. The new program aims to aid refugees by offering "important skills that will help them in the global economy," Evan Ryan, U.S. assistant secretary of state for educational and cultural affairs, said on a press call last week. "What we don't want to do is not act," added Coursera chief operations officer Lila Ibrahim. The idea isn't without problems. For one, starting a new career path isn't as simple as watching a few videos and obtaining an online certificate; even those looking to continue previous careers can't simply rely on an online lecture to get them up-to-date on standards, policies, and practices. For another, most of the classes on Coursera are in English, and though there are plans to add translations, language barriers can be a big obstacle. Then there are the questions over the value of massive open online courses (MOOCs) themselves—both for refugees and for average learners. But it's still early days and there are signs of hope. In 2015, a joint study found 72% of people taking the MOOCs saw career benefits afterwards.

To allow them to learn as many job skills as possible.

translation.source: 近年来,越来越多的年轻人喜爱各种形式的自助旅游。许多自助旅游者选择徒步或骑自行车出游。他们自 己设计路线,自带帐篷、厨具以及其他必备的生活用品。在旅途中,自助旅游者经常能够发现一些新的美丽景点, 但有时也会遇见意想不到的困难或突发事件。游客在旅行中拥抱自然、欣赏美景,同时也增强了自己克服困难 的勇气和野外生存的能力。
translation.reference: In recent years, more and more young people have become fond of various forms of self-guided travel. Many self-guided travelers choose to travel on foot or by bike. They design their own routes and bring their own tents, cooking utensils and other daily necessities. During their trips, self-guided travelers often discover some beautiful new scenic spots, but they sometimes encounter unexpected difficulties or emergencies. While embracing nature and enjoying the beautiful scenery during their trips, travelers also build up their courage to overcome difficulties and their ability to survive in the wild.
